Definition: from σκυθρός (sullen) and a derivative of G3700; angry-visaged, i.e. gloomy or affecting a mournful appearance:--of a sad countenance.
BiblicalUsage: Two kinds of sadness carry this word. On the road to Emmaus the two disciples walk along sad, unable to see who walks with them, and Jesus tells those who fast not to be of a sad countenance like the hypocrites, who disfigure their faces so men will see them fast.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe sadness is honest when it comes from a heavy heart, and false when it is worn for show, and the Lord sees the difference.
